narrative:
For nearly three decades, the City Council has churned out an astonishing 8,619 bills, a staggering number that underscores the complexity and nuance of local governance. From 2000 to 2025, this legislative body has been in constant motion, introducing and debating policies that shape the city's future. The sheer volume of legislation is a testament to the many issues facing our communities, from zoning regulations to infrastructure upgrades.

The data reveals some striking patterns. For instance, zoning laws have dominated the agenda, with 2,577 bills introduced over the years – a quarter of all legislation. This focus on land use and development reflects the city's ongoing struggle to balance growth with community needs. Another intriguing finding is the surprisingly high pass rate: an impressive 99% of closed bills have been signed into law, suggesting that the Council's deliberative process is generally effective in refining proposals. Additionally, the most active years for legislation reveal a cyclical pattern, with spikes in bill introduction during election years.

This data offers a unique window into the city's legislative history and highlights the importance of tracking policy developments. By understanding what issues receive attention and how priorities shift over time, residents can engage more effectively with their elected representatives. Open Common Ground makes it possible for citizens to navigate this vast dataset, empowering them to hold leaders accountable and advocate for change.
